children: The Dighi facility will target 2 million gross tonnes of annual shipbuilding capacity, supporting large commercial vessel construction in Maharashtra

Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders (MDL) will invest around Rs 27,000 crore to establish a greenfield shipbuilding cluster at Dighi in Maharashtra’s Raigad district. The project is expected to generate around 90,000 jobs, the Maharashtra government said on Tuesday.

MDL signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with National Shipbuilding and Heavy Industries Park Maharashtra Ltd (NSHIPML) in the presence of Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. The agreement is aimed at developing the proposed shipbuilding facility at Dighi, according to an official release.

As per the agreement, MDL has set a target of achieving an annual shipbuilding capacity of at least 2 million gross tonnes at Dighi. The project will enable the construction of large commercial vessels and strengthen the country’s maritime industrial capabilities, the release said.

The proposed Rs 27,000 crore investment will support the development of modern shipbuilding infrastructure at the site. It will also create an industrial and supply chain ecosystem aimed at supporting activities across the shipbuilding sector.

The greenfield shipbuilding cluster is being developed jointly by the Maharashtra Maritime Board and the Mumbai Port Authority through NSHIPML. The special-purpose company was established specifically to take forward the development of the proposed cluster.

The project is being taken forward under the Centre’s Greenfield Shipbuilding Cluster Development Plan and is expected to complement the objectives of the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. The initiative is expected to strengthen India’s maritime industrial capabilities.

According to the release, the Dighi project is expected to boost domestic shipbuilding capacity, attract technology and investment, and create skilled employment opportunities. It is also expected to enhance India’s competitiveness in the global maritime sector.

The proposed cluster will provide modern shipbuilding infrastructure alongside an industrial and supply chain ecosystem. The development is expected to support the wider maritime sector through increased capacity and related industrial activity.

MDL Chairman and Managing Director Captain Jagmohan said the company would work towards creating a modern, globally competitive shipbuilding facility at Dighi with the cooperation of all stakeholders. He said the facility would be developed with support from stakeholders involved in the project.

Captain Jagmohan signed the MoU with NSHIPML Managing Director Pradeep P, the release said. The agreement marks MDL’s proposed participation in the development of the Dighi greenfield shipbuilding cluster.
